title: Canary, Blue/Green & Shadow Deployment
interviewAnswer: Canary sends a small share of live traffic to the new model, blue/green switches between parallel environments, and shadow deployment mirrors traffic to a new model without using its outputs for users.
why: Safe deployment patterns reduce risk when a new model or service version behaves differently in production.
intuition: Blue/green keeps old and new environments side-by-side; canary sends a small fraction of real traffic to the new version; shadow mirrors traffic to the new version without using its response.
deepDive: Blue/green enables fast switch/rollback but duplicates capacity. Canary progressively increases exposure while monitoring metrics. Shadow tests production inputs safely but cannot fully measure user/business outcomes because responses are not served. A/B experiments are for causal product comparison, not just deployment safety. Model changes may require feature/schema compatibility across versions.
workedExample: Deploy v13 to 5% canary traffic, compare latency/errors and quality proxies to v12, then ramp 25→50→100% if gates pass; otherwise route all traffic back to v12.
commonMistakes: Calling a canary an A/B test automatically.
Running shadow traffic with side-effecting tools/actions.
Planning rollback without keeping the previous artifact/config ready.
followUps: How do database/schema changes complicate rollback?
production: Automate health gates and traffic rollback, but keep human approval for high-risk models. Ensure observability distinguishes metrics by model version.
